method: OPEN AND QUOTED from Jensen RT, Ramos-Alvarez I et al. (US National Institutes of Health), Biomedicines 'Current Medical Controversies in Zollinger–Ellison Syndrome' (2025). Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: CC BY 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC12730841). The ENETS 2023 guidance paper for functioning pancreatic NET syndromes (J Neuroendocrinol, DOI 10.1111/jne.13318, CC BY-NC-ND) was the preferred source but the Wiley page returned a bot challenge (HTTP 403), which was not bypassed; this review summarises its gastrinoma diagnostic recommendations.

claims.claim: ZES is gastric acid hypersecretion from ectopic gastrin secretion by a neuroendocrine tumour (gastrinoma), causing severe peptic ulcer disease or reflux that is often refractory to standard treatment.
claims.source_text: is characterized by gastric acid hypersecretion due to ectopic secretion of gastrin by a neuroendocrine tumor (NET) (gastrinoma) resulting in severe peptic ulcer disease (PUD)/gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), which is often refractory to standard PUD treatments
claims.locator: Jensen RT, Ramos-Alvarez I et al. (US National Institutes of Health), Biomedicines, 'Current Medical Controversies in Zollinger–Ellison Syndrome', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12730841/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: Gastrinomas are not curable by surgery in >50% of cases, mainly because of advanced or multifocal (MEN1) disease, so most patients need lifelong acid antisecretory drugs.
claims.source_text: gastrinomas, unfortunately, similar to other F-pNET syndromes, but different from insulinoma, are not curable in >50% of the cases, primarily because of the presence of advanced disease or multifocal (Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia-type-1[MEN-1]) disease … most patients require lifelong acid antisecretory medications to control their gastric acid hypersecretion
claims.locator: Jensen RT, Ramos-Alvarez I et al. (US National Institutes of Health), Biomedicines, 'Current Medical Controversies in Zollinger–Ellison Syndrome', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12730841/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: MEN1 is present in 20–25% of all ZES patients; MEN1/ZES patients usually have multiple, often small duodenal gastrinomas and a very low surgical cure rate.
claims.source_text: Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 1 (MEN1) (MEN1/ZES), which is 20-25% of all ZES patients … MEN1/ZES patients have, in the vast majority, multiple, frequently small gastrinomas in the duodenum associated with >50% having lymph node metastases, resulting in them having a very low surgical cure rate
claims.locator: Jensen RT, Ramos-Alvarez I et al. (US National Institutes of Health), Biomedicines, 'Current Medical Controversies in Zollinger–Ellison Syndrome', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12730841/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ Hyperparathyroidism is present in >95% of MEN1/ZES patients and can increase gastrin release and acid output and make acid harder to suppress medically.
claims.source_text: The concomitant presence of hyperparathyroidism, which is present in >95% of MEN1/ZES patients due to the parathyroid hyperplasia characteristically seen in MEN1 patients [,], can directly affect the behavior of the gastrinoma by stimulating the release of gastrin, increasing the basal acid output, affecting gastrin provocative secretin test positivity used in ZES diagnosis, and by increasing the difficulty in suppressing the acid secretion by medical therapy
claims.locator: Jensen RT, Ramos-Alvarez I et al. (US National Institutes of Health), Biomedicines, 'Current Medical Controversies in Zollinger–Ellison Syndrome', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12730841/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: The first test is usually a fasting serum gastrin (FSG); it is raised in >99% of ZES but has low specificity, because atrophic gastritis/pernicious anaemia, PPI use and H. pylori also raise gastrin.
claims.source_text: Almost invariably, the first study performed when the diagnosis of ZES is suspected is a FSG assay [,]. FSG levels are elevated in almost all patients with ZES (>99%), except in some rare circumstances, such as post-parathyroidectomy in MEN1/ZES or post-noncurative gastrinoma resection [,]. Unfortunately, while the FSG level has a very high sensitivity for diagnosing ZES it has low specificity … In humans the principal disorders causing physiological hypergastrinemia are chronic atrophic gastritis [CAG]/pernicious anemia, the use of PPIs, or the presence of H. pylori infections
claims.locator: Jensen RT, Ramos-Alvarez I et al. (US National Institutes of Health), Biomedicines, 'Current Medical Controversies in Zollinger–Ellison Syndrome', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12730841/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ PPIs cause hypergastrinaemia in 80–100% of users, starting within 5 days, and control symptoms of most ZES patients at ordinary doses, so PPI use both mimics and masks ZES.
claims.source_text: is that 80-100% develop PPI-induced hypergastrinemia [,]. Hypergastrinemia develops rapidly after starting PPI treatment (within 5 days) … PPIs control symptoms in most ZES patients at conventional doses used in the treatment of idiopathic PUD/GERD or they are frequently used for UGI symptoms in non-ZES patients [,]. In contrast to PPIs, with longterm treatment with H2R antagonists in ZES patients, higher dosing and/or more frequent dosing, are almost always needed than they are generally used to treat the typical patient with idiopathic GERD/PUD [,], thus helping to raise the suspicion that the patient may have ZES as a possible diagnosis. Hence, in the past when ZES patients were treated with the conventional doses of H2R antagonists which were widely used in non-ZES patients, they continued to have symptoms, raising the possible awareness that they may have ZES. However, this very important clinical observation that suggested the correct diagnosis of ZES is not with PPIs treatment [,]. The result of this combination of differences is that the use of PPIs greatly complicates the diagnosis of ZES
claims.locator: Jensen RT, Ramos-Alvarez I et al. (US National Institutes of Health), Biomedicines, 'Current Medical Controversies in Zollinger–Ellison Syndrome', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12730841/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ENETS guidance (as summarised): diagnose gastrinoma with FSG > 10× ULN plus gastric fluid pH ≤ 2 off PPIs; if FSG is 1–10× raised, do upper endoscopy with endoscopic ultrasound, CT or MRI, and somatostatin receptor imaging.
claims.source_text: one must demonstrate an FSG level > 10× ULN and a gastric fluid pH ≤ 2 in the absence of PPI use (classical definition = Table 1 (Part A)). In clinically suspected patients with FSG increased 1-10× URL, it is recommended a UGI endoscopy with an endoscopic ultrasound evaluation (EUS) be performed, as well as a CT or MRI examination and an SRI examination.
claims.locator: Jensen RT, Ramos-Alvarez I et al. (US National Institutes of Health), Biomedicines, 'Current Medical Controversies in Zollinger–Ellison Syndrome', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12730841/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: A secretin test increase in serum gastrin of ≥ 120 pg/mL had 94% sensitivity and 100% specificity for ZES, but secretin is not readily available in many centres.
claims.source_text: the best criterion for a positive test in ZES patients was an increase in serum gastrin with secretin ≥ 120 pg/mL, which had a sensitivity of 94% and specificity of 100% for identifying ZES patients … Unfortunately, in many centers/hospitals, secretin is not readily available and so, at present, it is uncommonly used.
claims.locator: Jensen RT, Ramos-Alvarez I et al. (US National Institutes of Health), Biomedicines, 'Current Medical Controversies in Zollinger–Ellison Syndrome', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12730841/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ Stopping PPIs abruptly for testing is risky: severe peptic and reflux complications have been reported in ZES patients.
claims.source_text: There have been a number of reports of severe gastric peptic/GERD complications in ZES patients after abruptly stopping PPIs
claims.locator: Jensen RT, Ramos-Alvarez I et al. (US National Institutes of Health), Biomedicines, 'Current Medical Controversies in Zollinger–Ellison Syndrome', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12730841/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: A raised gastrin with a positive somatostatin receptor scan is not specific for ZES, especially in MEN1 patients taking PPIs; serum chromogranin A has low specificity too.
claims.source_text: used the criteria for diagnosis of an elevated FSG combined with a positive SRI study [], this is not specific for ZES … This may be particularly true in MEN1 patients suspected of having ZES while taking a PPI, because these patients develop numerous neuroendocrine tumors in numerous locations, which can be positive on SRI, but which are not gastrinomas. … numerous studies have shown its usefulness is greatly limited in ZES patients, similarly to other patients with NETs/pNETs, because of its low specificity
claims.locator: Jensen RT, Ramos-Alvarez I et al. (US National Institutes of Health), Biomedicines, 'Current Medical Controversies in Zollinger–Ellison Syndrome', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12730841/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: Refer suspected patients to a centre with ZES expertise so the diagnosis is firmly established by the classical criteria.
claims.source_text: The best method to ensure this, at present, is to refer these patients to a center that has expertise in the diagnosis of ZES to firmly establish the diagnosis by the established classical criteria.
claims.locator: Jensen RT, Ramos-Alvarez I et al. (US National Institutes of Health), Biomedicines, 'Current Medical Controversies in Zollinger–Ellison Syndrome', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12730841/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: PPIs are the antisecretory drugs of choice, largely replacing H2-receptor antagonists because of greater potency and longer action.
claims.source_text: Currently, proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) have become the antisecretory drugs of choice to treat the acid hypersecretion in these patients, largely replacing the use of histamine H2-receptor antagonists (H2R), because of their increased potency and long duration of actions
claims.locator: Jensen RT, Ramos-Alvarez I et al. (US National Institutes of Health), Biomedicines, 'Current Medical Controversies in Zollinger–Ellison Syndrome', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12730841/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ Uncontrolled acid hypersecretion carries very high morbidity and mortality from acid-peptic complications, so control it rapidly.
claims.source_text: if the acid hypersecretion was not rapidly controlled these patients had very high morbidity and mortality due to uncontrolled acid-peptic complications
claims.locator: Jensen RT, Ramos-Alvarez I et al. (US National Institutes of Health), Biomedicines, 'Current Medical Controversies in Zollinger–Ellison Syndrome', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12730841/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: In the NIH series of 303 ZES patients treated for a mean of 13.7 yrs, medical control of hypersecretion succeeded in all patients, with each dose titrated individually; the PPI daily dose could be reduced over time in 47%.
claims.source_text: of long-term control of acid hypersecretion in 303 ZES patients treated for a mean of 13.7 yrs (range 0.08-48.1 yrs), in which medical control of the hypersecretion was successful in all patients both acutely and long-term. … could actually be decreased in 47% and 13% of the patients … which was performed by titrating each drug dose individually for each patient each year
claims.locator: Jensen RT, Ramos-Alvarez I et al. (US National Institutes of Health), Biomedicines, 'Current Medical Controversies in Zollinger–Ellison Syndrome', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12730841/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: Because acid secretory testing is rarely available, the authors recommend care in a specialty centre that can assess acid control, including symptom review and regular upper GI endoscopy on treatment.
claims.source_text: ZES patients for best care should be referred to a specialty center that has either the capability of assessing acid control status of antisecretory drugs or has developed other local criteria that allow long-term successful monitoring of the acid secretory control. These include centers having expertise in performing a careful history of acid-peptic/GERD symptoms, diarrhea, and overall health; the performance of regular UGI endoscopic assessments to establish lack of PUD/GERD findings on anti-secretory drugs
claims.locator: Jensen RT, Ramos-Alvarez I et al. (US National Institutes of Health), Biomedicines, 'Current Medical Controversies in Zollinger–Ellison Syndrome', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12730841/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: Long-term PPI treatment in ZES has been linked to hypomagnesaemia and low vitamin B12 stores; one patient's refractory hypomagnesaemia required total gastrectomy.
claims.source_text: (particularly hypomagnesemia and low vitamin B12 stores/vitamin B12 deficiency), which have led to difficulties in long term acid control and even the need for total gastrectomy
claims.locator: Jensen RT, Ramos-Alvarez I et al. (US National Institutes of Health), Biomedicines, 'Current Medical Controversies in Zollinger–Ellison Syndrome', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12730841/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: Hypomagnesaemia appears to be a PPI class effect: it resolves when PPIs stop, may recur with another PPI, but not with H2-receptor antagonists. In NIH ZES patients the rate was 0.4%.
claims.source_text: When PPI use is stopped, the hypomagnesemia disappears and, in some cases, recurs when the PPIs were restarted [,]. Evidence suggests the development of the hypomagnesemia is a general PPI class-effect, because its redevelopment has been reported with the subsequent use of other PPIs, but not when histamine H2-receptor antagonists were subsequently used … which resulted in a rate of 0.4% in the >300 patients chronically treated
claims.locator: Jensen RT, Ramos-Alvarez I et al. (US National Institutes of Health), Biomedicines, 'Current Medical Controversies in Zollinger–Ellison Syndrome', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12730841/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ Vitamin B12 deficiency developed in 21% of 175 NIH ZES patients over a mean 10.2 years, linked to PPI acid suppression; no patient on H2-receptor antagonists alone developed it.
claims.source_text: of 175 ZES patients from the NIH … found that over this treatment period of mean 10.2 yrs (5.6 yrs with PPIs) 21% of the ZES patients developed VB12 deficiency … In addition, no patient taking H2Rs in this study developed VB12 deficiency
claims.locator: Jensen RT, Ramos-Alvarez I et al. (US National Institutes of Health), Biomedicines, 'Current Medical Controversies in Zollinger–Ellison Syndrome', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12730841/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: Oral multivitamins containing crystalline vitamin B12 raised serum B12 by a mean of 34% without changing the PPI dose, suggesting deficiency can be easily avoided.
claims.source_text: In all the patients the serum VB12 level increased by a mean of 34% (p = 0.003) … suggests that VB12 deficiency can be easily avoided in these patients with the concomitant use of oral multivitamins
claims.locator: Jensen RT, Ramos-Alvarez I et al. (US National Institutes of Health), Biomedicines, 'Current Medical Controversies in Zollinger–Ellison Syndrome', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12730841/, retrieved 2026-09-23
